newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close lower on weaker beef.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close lower on weaker beef.

text.p: Further weakness in cash beef and evening up ahead of Friday's Cattle-on-Feed report kept CME live cattle futures pressured at the close. Feeders continued to follow the lead of deferred live cattle and also ended lower despite lower corn futures, traders said.

October fell on pressure from the recent setback in boxed beef values, with rolling of longs into back months and profit-taking ahead of the report weighing on prices. Concern over heavier cattle numbers into next year continued to pressure December which also fell when sell-stops were hit earlier, traders said.
But traders were unceratin if Thursday's action can be viewed as a market trend with the cattle report so close.
"I dont' want to read too much into price action today and tomorrow with that report coming," said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst for Brock Associates Inc.

Projections on Friday's report for on-feed cattle supplies as of September 1 in the seven key states averaged 89.9 percent and ranged from 88.2 to 92 percent of a year ago. The number of cattle placed in feedlots averaged 112.7 percent in a range of 106.6 to 119 percent and marketings averaged 94.7 percent in a range of 92 to 98 percent of a year ago.

"The cash fed cattle market and therefore the nearby, I think, are on pretty solid ground. October will stay aligned with cash and looks like we are going to be in this marketing hole for another three or four weeks," he said.
But Harper said deferreds look technically weak. "The charts suggest that maybe we have run the course with this (recent) up move in back months," he added.
Refco bought October at the close after selling early. Cargill Investor Services also bought October while selling February. R.J. O'Brien was a buyer much of the session, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, there was hedge interest, buying puts and selling calls in December and February and some selling of February 60 puts and 68 calls. Volatility was steady to strong, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures continued to follow the lead of deferred live cattle contracts and retreated late despite weakness in corn futures and discount to index, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.325 to 0.100 cent lower with October off most at 72.500 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.025 to 0.275 lower with October off 0.225 at 63.950 cents.
